channel.title: PsyDigest — psychiatry literature digest
channel.description: Summaries of new psychiatric research and guidelines

item.title: Prediction models for postpartum post-traumatic stress disorder: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis (PROSPERO protocol not stated) evaluated multivariable prediction models for postpartum PTSD within 12 months after delivery, aiming to quantify diagnostic accuracy and identify methodological gaps that limit clinical use.
FINDINGS: Seventeen studies (n=17 236) yielded a pooled AUC of 0.84 (95 % CI 0.80–0.88), sensitivity 0.77 and specificity 0.82. Predictors most often included mode of delivery, social support, pregnancy complications and fear of childbirth. High heterogeneity (I² = 89.7 %) and sparse calibration and external validation were noted.
INTERPRETATION: The models show encouraging discrimination, but the evidence base is weakened by substantial heterogeneity, incomplete reporting of calibration and few external validations. Without standardized development (e.g., TRIPOD adherence) and large multi-centre validations, the pooled metrics overstate likely real-world performance and generalisability.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current prediction models should not yet be implemented in routine maternity care; they remain research tools until rigorous external validation and calibration are demonstrated.

item.title: Clinical outcomes of early versus standard liver transplantation in patients with alcohol-related liver disease: a meta-analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study addresses whether early liver transplantation (eLT) without a mandatory 6-month abstinence period improves outcomes compared to standard liver transplantation (sLT) in patients with alcohol-related liver disease (ALD). This meta-analysis synthesizes observational and comparative studies to evaluate survival, relapse, graft outcomes, and hospitalization.
FINDINGS: Twelve studies (n=2323) showed no significant difference in mortality (RR=0.94, 95% CI: 0.73–1.22) or patient survival (HR=1.10, 95% CI: 0.83–1.45) between eLT and sLT. Alcohol relapse was more frequent after eLT but not significant in the primary analysis (RR=1.37, 95% CI: 0.95–2.00), though it became significant in sensitivity analyses. Acute graft rejection was higher with eLT (RR=1.22, 95% CI: 0.98–1.52), while graft loss was similar (RR=0.97, 95% CI: 0.74–1.27). Infection risk did not differ (RR=1.19, 95% CI: 0.80–1.77), but hospitalization was longer by 5.24 days (95% CI: 0.15–10.33).
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is limited to retrospective and cohort studies with potential selection bias and confounding. The pooled results suggest no survival advantage for eLT, but sensitivity analyses hint at higher relapse and rejection risks. The small effect sizes and wide confidence intervals reduce certainty. The longer hospitalization is a consistent finding but may reflect clinical caution rather than inherent risk. Overall, the evidence is preliminary and heterogeneous; definitive conclusions require prospective randomized trials.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Early LT appears to offer survival comparable to standard LT, supporting its consideration in carefully selected patients with severe ALD who fail medical therapy. Clinicians should be vigilant for higher relapse and rejection rates and plan for longer post-transplant care. Current practice should remain individualized and multidisciplinary until stronger evidence emerges.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Deep Learning Approaches for Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder Diagnosis: Protocol for a Scoping Review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study is a scoping review protocol aiming to map the evidence on AI, machine learning (ML), and deep learning (DL) approaches for diagnosing ADHD, addressing the current subjective diagnostic methods and the growing but fragmented research in this area. The review will include empirical studies published between January 2019 and April 2026, focusing on studies with sample sizes >100 participants and non-ADHD control groups.
FINDINGS: The scoping review will synthesize findings on model performance, data modalities (e.g., neuroimaging, electrophysiology, digital biomarkers), validation practices, and interpretability methods. It will use the Joanna Briggs Institute approach and PRISMA-ScR guidelines, with screening and analysis currently in progress and expected completion in June 2026.
INTERPRETATION: As a scoping review protocol, this study does not present results but outlines a rigorous methodology to map the landscape of AI-based ADHD diagnostic tools. The strength lies in its comprehensive search strategy and predefined inclusion criteria, but the findings will depend on the quality and heterogeneity of the included studies. The review will highlight gaps in validation practices and clinical translation readiness, which are critical for future research and potential clinical implementation.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This review will not change clinical practice immediately but will provide a foundation for future AI-based diagnostic tools by identifying the most promising data modalities, validation methods, and interpretability approaches. Clinicians should watch for its findings to understand the current state of AI in ADHD diagnosis and potential future applications.

item.title: Early interventions for primary care patients with stress-related mental ill health: a randomised controlled non-inferiority trial of a nurse-led collaborative care intervention versus cognitive behavioural therapy.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The trial asked whether a nurse-led collaborative care (CC) model is no worse than psychologist-guided self-help cognitive behavioural therapy (GSH-CBT) for reducing stress in adult primary care patients with mild-to-moderate stress-related mental ill-health. It was a 12-week, two-arm, non-inferiority RCT (n = 172).
FINDINGS: Both groups improved substantially on the Perceived Stress Scale-10 (PSS-10) and all secondary measures. The between-group effect on PSS-10 was small (d = 0.22, 95 % CI –0.09 to 0.52), with the upper bound exceeding the pre-set non-inferiority margin of 0.3 d. GSH-CBT showed a slightly larger reduction in exhaustion (d = 0.28, 95 % CI 0.002 to 0.56). No other between-group differences reached statistical significance.
INTERPRETATION: The study met its internal validity requirements (randomisation, allocation concealment, intention-to-treat analysis), but the non-inferiority margin was crossed, so CC cannot be declared non-inferior to GSH-CBT. The observed differences are small and of uncertain clinical importance. External validity is reasonable for Swedish primary care, yet generalisability may be limited by the exclusion of severe cases and reliance on self-report measures.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Nurse-led CC remains a safe, feasible option when psychologists are unavailable, but it is not demonstrably equivalent to GSH-CBT; clinicians should still prioritise access to CBT where possible.

item.title: Retinal Biomarkers of Cognition in Schizophrenia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review and meta-analysis (k=16 studies, n=847 patients) examined whether retinal layer thinning in schizophrenia correlates with cognitive deficits across domains such as overall cognition, attention, processing speed, and executive function, using optical coherence tomography (OCT) measures.
FINDINGS: Pooled correlations showed small but statistically significant associations between thinner retinal layers and poorer cognition: overall cognition with macular-retinal nerve fiber layer (mRNFL; pooled-r=0.180; p=.002; k=7) and superior peripapillary RNFL (pRNFL; pooled-r=0.214; p=.026; k=7). Attention correlated with mRNFL (r=0.210; p<.001; k=6), macular-inner plexiform layer (mIPL; r=0.142; p=.012; k=8), and pRNFL (r=0.207; p<.001; k=9). Processing speed correlated with foveal thickness (r=0.206; p=.008; k=7), mIPL (r=0.194; p=.001; k=6), and pRNFL (r=0.211; p<.001; k=5). Executive function correlated with macular thickness (r=0.099; p=.018; k=10) and mRNFL (r=0.159; p=.009; k=6). Age, sex, cardiometabolic comorbidities, and smoking moderated these effects.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests a modest association between retinal thinning and cognitive impairment in schizophrenia, but the small effect sizes (r≈0.14–0.21) and limited number of studies (k≤10 per domain) mean results should be interpreted cautiously. Heterogeneity in OCT protocols, cognitive assessments, and patient characteristics limits comparability. No causal inference can be drawn, and confounding by illness severity or treatment exposure remains possible.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Retinal OCT is non-invasive and widely available, but current evidence does not support its use as a standalone biomarker for cognitive deficits in schizophrenia. Further longitudinal, well-controlled studies are needed before considering clinical integration.

item.title: CO-produced Nature-based Intervention Feasibility for children with ADHD Study: The CONIFAS2 study protocol.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The CONIFAS2 study is a feasibility randomised controlled trial (RCT) examining whether a co-produced, home-based nature-based intervention (NBI) is acceptable and feasible for children with ADHD and their families within UK NHS neurodiversity services, compared to treatment as usual (TAU). The study addresses unmet post-diagnostic support needs and under-researched adjunctive interventions.
FINDINGS: The trial will recruit children with ADHD and their parent/guardian dyads from NHS services and randomise them to either NBI plus TAU or TAU alone. Key feasibility outcomes include recruitment and retention rates, intervention fidelity, data completeness, and acceptability of both the intervention and trial procedures. A mixed-methods process evaluation will explore barriers and facilitators to delivery and engagement, while a feasibility health economic evaluation will assess the practicality of collecting cost and quality-of-life data for future cost-effectiveness analysis.
INTERPRETATION: As a feasibility RCT, this study is not powered to detect clinical efficacy but aims to establish whether a definitive trial is viable. Strengths include its pragmatic NHS setting and co-production approach, which may enhance external validity. However, limitations include the lack of a control group receiving an active comparator, potential selection bias in recruitment from neurodiversity services, and the absence of blinding. The findings will clarify feasibility but will not determine clinical effectiveness or cost-effectiveness.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study could inform the design of future trials evaluating NBIs for ADHD, but it does not yet provide evidence to change clinical practice. Clinicians should await results from a definitive trial before considering NBIs as adjunctive treatments in routine care.

item.title: Cross-ancestry and cross-disorder transferability of polygenic risk scores for obsessive-compulsive disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional genetic study examined whether polygenic risk scores (PRSs) derived from European genome-wide association studies (GWAS) for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) and other psychiatric disorders predict OCD status in an East Asian cohort (532 Korean cases, 4376 controls), and whether cross-ancestry PRSs improve prediction.
FINDINGS: The European OCD PRS showed a modest but significant association with Korean OCD status (best-fit R² = 1.17%). In multivariable models, OCD PRS (OR 1.28, 95% CI 1.13–1.45), schizophrenia PRS (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.03–1.32), and anorexia nervosa PRS (OR 1.17, 95% CI 1.03–1.32) were independently associated with OCD. A stepwise multi-PRS model including seven psychiatric disorders increased incremental R² to 2.99%. Cross-ancestry meta-analysis PRSs for bipolar disorder and schizophrenia outperformed single-ancestry PRSs (incremental R² 2.84% and 1.28%, respectively).
INTERPRETATION: The evidence is moderate in internal validity (well-powered discovery GWAS, multivariable adjustment, cross-ancestry comparison) but limited in external validity (single East Asian cohort, cross-sectional design, small effect sizes). The small R² values indicate that current PRSs explain only a tiny fraction of OCD variance, so clinical translation is not imminent. The study highlights shared genetic architecture between OCD and other psychiatric disorders, particularly schizophrenia and anorexia nervosa, but replication in larger, diverse cohorts and functional validation are needed.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: At present, PRSs for OCD have no immediate bedside utility for diagnosis, risk stratification, or treatment selection in routine psychiatric care; they remain a research tool to map genetic overlap across disorders.

item.title: Using multi-trait polygenic scores to predict lithium responsiveness in patients with bipolar disorder.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study evaluated whether combining multiple polygenic scores (PGSs) from phenotypes related to lithium response or bipolar disorder could better predict lithium responsiveness in patients with bipolar disorder. Using data from 2,367 participants in the International Consortium on Lithium Genetics study, the researchers developed a multi-trait PGS (mt-PGS) and assessed its predictive power using both continuous and categorical measures of lithium response.
FINDINGS: The mt-PGS explained 5.70% of the variability in lithium responsiveness when using the continuous Alda score and 9.11% when using the categorical outcome (favourable vs. unfavourable response). The model achieved a classification accuracy (area under the curve) of 68.24% (95% CI: 64.98–71.66) for the categorical outcome, with a Brier score of 0.257. The psychiatric and behavioural phenotype cluster contributed most strongly to prediction, accounting for 3.67–6.52% of variability in lithium response.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence suggests that combining multiple PGSs modestly improves prediction of lithium response compared to single-trait approaches, but the explained variance remains low (≤9.11%). The study’s strengths include a large sample size and rigorous machine learning methods, but limitations include the retrospective design, reliance on the Alda scale (which has inherent subjectivity), and lack of external validation. The clinical utility is currently limited due to the small effect size and modest classification accuracy.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: While this study advances the field by demonstrating incremental predictive value of mt-PGS, it does not yet support clinical implementation. Further research is needed to refine models, validate findings in diverse populations, and integrate genetic data with clinical factors before considering use in routine care.

item.title: A systematic review of hydrocephalus and psychiatric comorbidities in children and adults with spina bifida.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This PRISMA-compliant systematic review examined whether hydrocephalus in children and adults with spina bifida is associated with psychiatric comorbidities. The clinical question is whether hydrocephalus contributes to mental health problems in this population, and the review synthesized observational studies comparing those with and without hydrocephalus.
FINDINGS: Eight studies (total N = 1 860) were included. In three pediatric cohorts, hydrocephalus was linked to higher inattention and hyperactivity symptoms (no effect sizes or p-values reported). In five adult cohorts, findings were inconsistent, with no clear pattern of association between hydrocephalus and psychiatric diagnoses or symptoms.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is very small (≤8 studies per age group) and heterogeneous in design, populations, and outcome measures, limiting firm conclusions. The pediatric signal for ADHD-type symptoms is suggestive but not quantified; adult data are conflicting and inconclusive. Risk of bias and confounding (e.g., severity of spina bifida, shunt dependence, socioeconomic factors) were not systematically assessed. Funding sources were not reported.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not justify routine screening for psychiatric disorders based solely on the presence of hydrocephalus in spina bifida. Clinicians should maintain standard psychiatric assessment for all patients with spina bifida, especially children with inattention or hyperactivity, while recognizing that evidence for a hydrocephalus-specific risk is preliminary and inconsistent.

item.title: Metabolomics Methods for Detecting Acetaminophen Poisoning: A Systematic Review.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This systematic review examined whether metabolomics methods can detect biomarkers of liver injury in acetaminophen (APAP) poisoning earlier than conventional approaches. It synthesised 18 studies (n=1,503) using 24 metabolomics techniques to identify metabolic changes associated with APAP-induced hepatotoxicity.
FINDINGS: Across the 18 included studies, metabolomics identified multiple metabolic intermediates linked to glutathione depletion and mitochondrial dysfunction before overt cell death. Techniques varied widely (e.g., LC-MS, NMR), and seven studies were registered on clinicaltrials.gov. No trials were found on the Indian registry. The review highlights early detection potential but does not report pooled effect sizes or diagnostic accuracy metrics.
INTERPRETATION: The evidence base is preliminary and heterogeneous, with no standardised metabolomics protocol or validated biomarkers. The lack of registered trials outside the US/UK and absence of data integration tools limit generalisability. While biologically plausible, clinical utility remains unproven due to methodological variability and absence of head-to-head comparisons with standard liver function tests.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Current evidence does not support replacing standard APAP toxicity monitoring with metabolomics. Future research should focus on standardising methods, validating biomarkers, and demonstrating clinical utility in real-world settings before considering adoption in practice.

item.title: Changes in Multisystem Morbidity in Thyroid Cancer after the 2015 ATA Guideline: A Nationwide Population-Based Retrospective Cohort Study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: The study examined whether a less intensive, risk-adapted approach to thyroid cancer management introduced by the 2015 ATA guideline was associated with reduced non-cancer-specific multisystem morbidity in a nationwide retrospective cohort of patients who underwent total thyroidectomy in Korea (n = 126,184; pre-guideline 2009–2014, post-guideline 2016–2021).
FINDINGS: After 1:1 propensity score matching and multivariable Cox regression, the post-guideline period showed lower risks of composite skeletal outcomes (HR 0.83, 95 % CI 0.69–0.99) and composite neurocognitive/psychiatric outcomes (HR 0.73, 95 % CI 0.69–0.77). Composite cardiovascular/cerebrovascular outcomes were unchanged overall, but secondary analyses revealed lower risks of atrial fibrillation (HR 0.62, 95 % CI 0.50–0.76), myocardial infarction (HR 0.81, 95 % CI 0.66–0.99), and stroke (HR 0.56, 95 % CI 0.49–0.63). All-cause mortality did not differ between periods.
INTERPRETATION: The study’s large, population-based design and use of propensity matching strengthen internal validity, but residual confounding from unmeasured variables (e.g., changes in adjuvant therapy, lifestyle, or surveillance intensity) remains possible. The observed HRs suggest modest but statistically significant reductions in skeletal and neurocognitive/psychiatric morbidity and selected cardiovascular events; however, effect sizes are small and clinical significance may be limited. External validity is constrained by the Korean healthcare setting and specific thyroid cancer population.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: The findings support the safety and potential long-term benefits of guideline-driven de-intensification in thyroid cancer care, particularly regarding skeletal and psychiatric morbidity and certain cardiovascular outcomes. Clinicians should remain alert to subtle shifts in morbidity patterns and continue routine monitoring rather than altering practice based solely on these results.

item.title: Rising demand and NHS reforms: what are the implications for mental health service provision?
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This editorial examines the implications of England’s NHS 10-year plan for mental health services, which proposes three major shifts: hospital-to-community care, analogue-to-digital delivery, and sickness-to-prevention focus. It assesses how these reforms may impact mental health service provision across the life course.
FINDINGS: The editorial outlines policy intentions without presenting empirical data. It highlights the planned expansion of community-based services and digital tools, aiming to reduce reliance on inpatient care and improve early intervention. However, it notes concerns about workforce capacity, funding sustainability, and equitable access across regions.
INTERPRETATION: As an editorial, this is a narrative review without quantitative outcomes or systematic evidence synthesis. Its strength lies in contextualizing policy changes, but it lacks rigorous evaluation of effectiveness or implementation challenges. The discussion is speculative regarding real-world impact on patient outcomes or service quality.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This piece does not provide actionable clinical data but signals potential shifts in service models. Clinicians should monitor local service changes and advocate for evidence-based implementation of digital and community-based care to ensure quality and accessibility.

item.title: Psychiatric comorbidity, burden of sickness absence and sex-specific characteristics of working individuals with ADHD treated in primary care in the Finnish occupational health system: cross-sectional register study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This cross-sectional register study examined 2,117 working adults with ADHD in Finnish occupational health services (2018–2022) to describe psychiatric comorbidities, service use, medication patterns, and sex differences in sickness absence.
FINDINGS: Psychiatric comorbidity was present in 80.5% of patients, most commonly anxiety (51.8%) and depression (43.9%). Among 1,447 with complete data, 87.0% had seen a psychiatrist and 70.1% a psychologist. Men were more often treated with stimulants only (27.4% vs 18.4%), while women more often received antidepressants alone or combined with anxiolytics. Women had substantially higher psychiatric sickness absence across all durations: RRR 2.08 (95% CI 1.37–3.14) for 1–7 days, RRR 2.03 (1.42–2.90) for 8–30 days, and RRR 2.75 (2.16–3.52) for >30 days.
INTERPRETATION: The study provides robust real-world data on high comorbidity and service use in employed adults with ADHD, but its cross-sectional design precludes causal inference. The large sex differences in sickness absence are striking and clinically plausible, though residual confounding (e.g., unmeasured symptom severity) cannot be excluded. The effect sizes are large and clinically meaningful, but the study cannot determine whether different prescribing patterns drive the observed differences in work disability.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Clinicians should anticipate high psychiatric comorbidity and frequent specialist referrals in working adults with ADHD. Sex-specific prescribing patterns may reflect differing clinical presentations or treatment preferences; monitoring and supporting work ability—especially in women with ADHD—may be warranted.

item.title: Associations between lifestyle, genetic liability for severe mental illness and risk of incident somatic illnesses.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This large UK Biobank cohort study (n=315,313) examined whether modifiable lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol, diet, exercise) and polygenic risk scores (PRS) for schizophrenia (SCZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) independently or jointly predict incident somatic illnesses over a median 14-year follow-up.
FINDINGS: Healthy lifestyle was associated with lower risks of type 2 diabetes (T2D; HR 0.43), cardiovascular disease (CVD; HR 0.70), dementia (HR 0.56), rheumatoid arthritis (HR 0.80), asthma (HR 0.75), chronic liver disease (CLD; HR 0.60), and cancer (HR 0.75). Higher PRS-SCZ increased asthma (HR 1.06) and dementia (HR 1.04) risks but decreased T2D risk (HR 0.96). Higher PRS-BD increased T2D risk (HR 1.04). No significant additive interaction was found between genetic risk and lifestyle.
INTERPRETATION: The study demonstrates robust associations between healthy lifestyle and reduced somatic illness risk across multiple conditions, independent of genetic liability. Genetic risks showed outcome-specific effects, with PRS-SCZ and PRS-BD contributing independent information for T2D. Limitations include observational design (residual confounding), healthy volunteer bias in UK Biobank, and lack of PRS validation in non-European ancestry groups. The clinical significance of small HRs for genetic risks (e.g., 1.04–1.06) is uncertain.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: Lifestyle interventions remain a high-yield target for reducing somatic comorbidity in patients with or at genetic risk for SMI. Genetic risk stratification for somatic illness is not yet clinically actionable.

item.title: Association of lithium versus valproate initiation with all-cause mortality and incident dementia: a multinational real-world cohort study.
item.description:
BACKGROUND: This multinational real-world cohort study compared long-term risks of all-cause mortality and incident dementia among adults aged ≥40 initiating lithium versus valproate, addressing uncertainty about their comparative safety and cognitive outcomes.
FINDINGS: In a propensity score–matched cohort of 22,098 patients per group, lithium initiation was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.53–0.63) and incident dementia (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.60–0.76) over five years. Five-year cumulative event probabilities were 6.61% vs 10.65% for mortality and 3.51% vs 4.85% for dementia with lithium vs valproate.
INTERPRETATION: The study’s large, multinational real-world design strengthens external validity, and sensitivity analyses support robustness. However, residual confounding from unmeasured clinical and lifestyle factors is likely, and the data rely on recorded diagnoses rather than adjudicated outcomes. The effect sizes are modest and may not translate into large absolute benefits for individual patients.
CLINICAL RELEVANCE: These findings suggest lithium may have advantages over valproate for long-term mortality and dementia risk, but the observational design precludes causal inference; treatment choice should still weigh efficacy, tolerability, and patient-specific factors.

item.title: The Impact of Heterogeneity in Individual Characteristics and Motivation to Quit Heroin Use on Contingency Management and Opioid Agonist Treatment Response: A Latent Class Analysis.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Contingency Management (CM) involves the systematic application of positive reinforcement (financial incentives) to promote behaviour change, to improve treatment outcomes for individuals with opioid use disorder (OUD). To better understand patient heterogeneity, this study sought to identify meaningful subgroups/classes underlying the population based on characteristic groupings, followed by determining whether CM effectiveness varied between these subgroups.

item.title: The Philadelphia Theta Burst Project: A novel fMRI-guided electric field modeling dataset with reliability metrics.
item.description: Recent neuromodulation studies suggest that theta burst stimulation (TBS) applied to the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC) can influence neural circuits involved in cognitive control and emotion-related processing, with relevance for psychiatric disorders. However, large-scale datasets characterizing variability, reliability, and multimodal neural responses to TBS remain limited.

item.title: Prenatal stress reprograms placental signaling and opposes maternal immune activation effects in the fetal brain.
item.description: Prenatal psychosocial stress and maternal immune activation (MIA) increase risk for overlapping offspring psychiatric disorders, but whether they influence fetal neurodevelopment through shared or distinct mechanisms is unclear. Positioned at the interface of maternal and fetal physiology, the placenta has a critical role in regulating fetal brain development. Here, we combine mouse placental single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptomics of matched placentas and fetal brains, maternal cytokine profiling, and human placental RNA-seq to dissect this axis.

item.title: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder and Late-Life Cognitive Impairment.
item.description: IMPORTANCE: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) affects tens to hundreds of millions of adults worldwide, and preliminary evidence suggests it may be associated with increased risk of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and dementia. However, concerns regarding diagnostic ascertainment and residual confounding remain. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association of ADHD with incident cognitive impairment, defined as MCI or dementia, using electronic health record (EHR) diagnoses and genetic liability measured using genome-wide ADHD polygenic risk score (ADHD PRS) in the same individuals.

item.title: Self-medication as metaphor: why psychiatry should revise an (in)convenient narrative about substance use and mental disorders.
item.description: The term self-medication remains an influential narrative to explain why some patients with mental health problems use psychoactive substances. This Feature offers a conceptual critique of its broad use in psychiatry. We argue that self-medication often functions less as a testable explanatory model and more as a rhetorical metaphor: clinically convenient, yet scientifically under-specified and normatively loaded.

item.title: Enabling responsible industry-academic collaboration in mental health research and the involvement of people with lived experience.
item.description: There is an urgent need for more effective and better-tolerated treatments for mental illness. Achieving this requires responsible collaboration between academia, healthcare professionals, industry and people with lived experience. However, regulatory and compliance frameworks can make early-stage, non-promotional collaboration difficult, particularly when discussions are exploratory and multidisciplinary.

item.title: Mapping the genetic landscape of the age at onset and severity of eating disorder symptoms.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Eating disorder treatment is most successful when delivered at first onset, underscoring the importance of early intervention. Genetic factors may contribute to earlier onset, but molecular genetic research into symptom onset and severity remains limited. AIMS: We investigated: (a) age at onset of behavioural symptoms and low weight, including sex and gender differences; and (b) the single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP)-based heritability and cross-trait polygenic associations of symptoms, onset, and severity.

item.title: Surveying alternative transcripts of disease-associated genes and their cell type specificity - a case study with ANK3.
item.description: The ANK3 gene has been conclusively linked to bipolar disorder, but its role in disease etiology remains unclear: both the specific transcript and its expressing cell type remain unclear. This is a near-universal problem for genes associated with polygenic neuropsychiatric disorders. One of the causes of this unfortunate stasis is that human transcript databases have an incomplete list of alternative isoforms of genes and that it is technically challenging to identify the cell-types in which they are expressed. Here, we address this knowledge gap for ANK3.

item.title: The Relationship between Air Pollution Exposure, Genetic Liability for Schizophrenia, and Brain Outcomes in the ABCD Study.
item.description: BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Air pollution exposure has been associated with altered neurodevelopment and increased risk of schizophrenia. Individuals at high genetic risk may be more vulnerable to these effects. Here, we examined how air pollution relates to brain structure and functional connectivity in adolescents, and we tested for the first time whether genetic risk for schizophrenia exacerbates these effects.

item.title: Resilience Pathways in Psychosis.
item.description: BACKGROUND AND HYPOTHESIS: Risk factors for psychosis spectrum disorders have been studied for many years, but recent research has begun to focus on resilience factors that protect against illness onset and mitigate illness course. Understanding resilience pathways will help us to apply interventions that can prevent psychosis and/or significantly improve illness trajectory.

item.title: Decoding the Anxiety Burden in Asia and Developing an XGBoost-Based Online Screening Tool Using Korean Data.
item.description: Anxiety disorders impose a substantial burden across Asia, yet comprehensive regional surveillance remains limited. In addition, the utility of the Health-Related Quality of Life Instrument with 8 Items (HINT-8) for anxiety screening in the Korean population has not been fully clarified.

item.title: Perinatal mental health outcomes for people with intellectual disability: A data linkage study in New South Wales, Australia.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To describe perinatal mental health outcomes among people with intellectual disability giving birth in New South Wales, Australia. METHODS: This retrospective, descriptive cohort study included 30,257 people (2262 people with intellectual disability and 27,995 comparators without intellectual disability) aged 10+ years, discharged from New South Wales hospitals between 2002 and 2017 following a live singleton birth.

item.title: Cross-Disease Classification of Depression, Bipolar Disorder, and Schizophrenia Using Multiscale Spatiotemporal Network Fusion Features From fNIRS.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Major depressive disorder (MDD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SCZ) are highly prevalent and disabling psychiatric conditions with increasing incidence, significantly affecting individuals' daily functioning, social relationships, and overall quality of life. Current diagnostic practices largely rely on clinical interviews and symptom-based rating scales, which are inherently subjective and time-consuming-posing major obstacles to large-scale screening.

item.title: Effects of opioids and stimulants on the respiratory system.
item.description: Drug overdose remains an urgent public health concern as it is a leading cause of fatal injury in the United States, with approximately 90% being attributed to opioid-induced respiratory depression from synthetic opioids. This statistic is primarily driven by the rise in the use of fentanyl, a potent synthetic opioid and its increased use in combination with stimulant drugs. The rise in the combined use of opioids and stimulants raises questions about pharmacological and physiological interactions, and its implication for the treatment of their addictive consequences and of overdoses.

item.title: Impact of alcohol abstinence on hepatic enzymes: A clinical analysis at the rehabilitation center of Kathmandu.
item.description: ObjectiveAlcoholic liver disease is a major cause of liver-related mortality, accounting for approximately half of cirrhosis-related deaths. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of alcohol abstinence on liver enzyme alterations.MethodsThis prospective cohort study was conducted over 8 months at Amrita Foundation, Kathmandu, and involved patients with alcohol dependence syndrome who had confirmed alcoholic liver disease. A structured questionnaire was used for data collection.

item.title: Longitudinal Risk Factors for Incident Lung Cancer Among a Mixed HIV Serostatus Cohort of Sexual Minority Men in the United States.
item.description: To examine how the co-occurrence of behavioral and psychosocial factors (depression, cigarette smoking, heavy alcohol use, and polydrug use) is associated with lung cancer incidence, we included 3,554 sexual minority men (SMM) from the Multicenter AIDS Cohort Study (MACS), 1996-2022, with assessments every 6 months. We used Cox proportional hazards models to examine the cumulative relationships of these factors with lung cancer incidence. We identified a positive dose-response relationship between the number of these factors and lung cancer incidence.

item.title: Defining psychosocial distress in pregnancy with fetal anomaly: A Delphi consensus study to identify core domains.
item.description: OBJECTIVE: To define psychosocial distress in pregnancies affected by fetal anomaly and identify its core domains and indicators. METHODS: We conducted a three-round Delphi study with an expert panel of individuals with lived experience of pregnancy with fetal anomaly and maternal-fetal care professionals. Round 1 open-ended responses were analyzed using directed content analysis and integrated with the literature to generate an initial indicator pool.

item.title: Psychiatric, anesthetic, and procedural characteristics of modified electroconvulsive therapy courses in adolescents treated in a tertiary child and adolescent psychiatry service: a 15-year retrospective cohort study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Evidence on electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) in adolescents is largely retrospective and rarely reports psychiatric outcomes together with anesthetic and procedural characteristics. We characterized modified ECT courses in a tertiary child and adolescent psychiatry service. METHODS: This retrospective cohort included adolescents aged 13-18 years treated with modified ECT from 2010 to 2025; the ECT course was the unit of analysis. Illness severity was rated with the Clinical Global Impression-Severity (CGI-S) scale at admission and discharge.

item.title: Fregoli syndrome in an adolescent with Moyamoya disease.
item.description: Moyamoya disease (MMD) is a progressive cerebrovascular disorder characterised by distal internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis and compensatory collateral vessel formation. Psychiatric manifestations are rare, particularly in children. We report the case of an early adolescent with previously diagnosed MMD who developed acute-onset psychosis following a febrile illness associated with headache and vomiting.

item.title: Psychosocial and structural factors associated with postpartum depressive symptoms and maternal continuum of care in Borama, Somaliland: a cross-sectional study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Postpartum depression (PPD) and fragmented maternal care are critical public health challenges in sub-Saharan Africa. OBJECTIVE: To examine the associations of psychosocial, structural, clinical, and health-system factors with self-reported postpartum depressive symptoms and maternal continuum-of-care (CoC) completion in Borama, Somaliland. METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional study analyzed 442 postnatal women. Postpartum depressive symptoms were assessed via binary self-report, and CoC was summarized using a 0-3 index (ANC4+, facility delivery, and postnatal care).

item.title: A multi-omics perspective on bipolar disorder.
item.description: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a complex mood disorder with multifactorial biological origins, and omics research has been playing a central role in unraveling its molecular signatures. This chapter provides a descriptive overview of current multi-omics findings in BD, integrating evidence from genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and metallomics.

item.title: Co-creating and testing a bibliotherapy e-storybook for children coping with parental complex post-traumatic stress disorder.
item.description: Background: Children living with a parent with complex post-traumatic stress disorder (CPTSD) may struggle to understand and respond to parental behaviours, increasing their risk of distress and mental health difficulties. Despite this, few evidence-informed narrative resources exist to support these children.Method: A free bibliotherapy e-storybook was co-created with over 30 participants from the affected communities and partners, including individuals with lived experience, service providers, clinicians, and an international interdisciplinary research team.

item.title: Mental Health Changes Among LGBTQIA+ Persons After the 2024 US Presidential Election.
item.description: Objectives. To determine whether mental health has changed among lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, intersex, asexual, and other sexual or gender minority (LGBTQIA+) people in the United States since the November 2024 election. Methods. This longitudinal observational cohort study of LGBTQIA+ people in the United States (n = 2150) examined changes in mental health symptoms (depression, anxiety, posttraumatic stress disorder) from before (June 2023-May 2024) to after (November 2024-July 2025) the November 2024 election using fixed-effects models. Results.

item.title: Nitrous Oxide Use in Autistic Children: A Descriptive Study.
item.description: OBJECTIVES: Describe the population of autistic children who undergo nitrous oxide sedation and the rate of associated adverse events (AEs). Analyze patient- and procedure-level factors associated with AEs in autistic children receiving nitrous oxide outside the dental setting. METHODS: A retrospective, descriptive study of autistic children, 3 to 18 years, who received nitrous oxide for procedural sedation during an emergency department or sedation encounter within a single hospital system between January 2014 and December 2023.

item.title: Implementation of components of a family navigation program for children with autism in a pediatric clinic: a best practice implementation project.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Early diagnosis and intervention assists children with autism to reach their full potential. Children in rural areas experience extended wait times for early intervention, and parents are often concerned about meeting their child's needs with minimal support during the waiting period. Family navigation programs can help fill this gap, providing tools and emotional support to parents while waiting for early intervention to begin.

item.title: Objective and Subjective Voice Assessment in Children With Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder.
item.description: INTRODUCTION: The aim of this study was to compare acoustic voice measures, auditory-perceptual voice quality, and parent-reported voice handicap between children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and typically developing (TD) peers. STUDY DESIGN: Case-control study.

item.title: Eating Behavior Profiles and Associated Factors in Children with ADHD: A Multidimensional and Multi-Informant Perspective.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) has been associated with atypical eating behaviors and weight-related outcomes in childhood; however, relationships between specific ADHD symptom dimensions and distinct eating behavior patterns across informants remain insufficiently characterized. This study compared eating behaviors between children with ADHD and typically developing peers and examined symptom-specific correlates of food-approach and food-avoidance behaviors.

item.title: Altered pain processing and associated neural circuitry disruptions in adolescents with early-onset psychosis.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Abnormal pain processing and somatosensory aversions are underappreciated clinical features of early onset psychosis (EOP). We aimed to identify their clinical, neurobehavioral, and brain circuit level correlates. METHODS: Clinical assessments and child (ages 12-18 years) and parent-reported outcomes were administered to adolescents with EOP (N = 31) and compared to chronic pain (CP, N = 27), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD, N = 30), and healthy control (HCs, N = 20) cohorts.

item.title: Pathological Priming and Developmental Heterochrony as Organizing Concepts in Human iPSC Models of Autism Spectrum Disorder.
item.description: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition in which diverse genetic risk factors converge on molecular pathways governing early brain development. Human-induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) and brain organoid models now permit direct interrogation of these pathways in patient-derived neural tissue and, in a subset of studies, reveal alterations in neural progenitor proliferation, cortical neurogenesis, synaptic maturation, and network excitability.

item.title: Recent Advances in Autism Spectrum Disorder Research on Epigenetics and Personalised Medicine.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a multifaceted neurodevelopmental condition characterised by impairments in social interaction and communication, repetitive and restricted patterns of behaviour and atypical sensory processing. Although genetic susceptibility accounts for a substantial proportion of ASD risk, increasing evidence indicates that epigenetic modifications and environmental exposures play pivotal roles in disease development and progression.

item.title: Effects of High-Phenolic Extra Virgin Olive Oil on Sensory Processing in Children With Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Pilot Study.
item.description: No approved treatments currently exist for the core symptoms of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), prompting clinicians and families to seek alternative approaches, including dietary and nutritional interventions. The Mediterranean diet (MeDi), characterized by a high intake of antioxidant and anti-inflammatory components, is associated with improved health outcomes and reduced risk of chronic diseases. A key element of the MeDi is extra virgin olive oil (EVOO), which is rich in bioactive phenolics, including oleocanthal, oleuropein and hydroxytyrosol.

item.title: Estimating Network Adequacy of Autism Service Providers in Affordable Care Act Markets.
item.description: UNLABELLED: In the past two decades, behavioral health care for children on the autism spectrum has changed considerably. As demand for applied behavior analysis (ABA) services escalated, government policies broadened health insurance coverage and the number of Board Certified Behavior Analysts increased. Yet, the network adequacy of these providers is unknown. Applying new Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) distance standards, we estimated county-level network adequacy in Affordable Care Act plan markets.

item.title: From Innovation to Impact: The CREATE Framework as a Blueprint for Large Language Model Adoption in Opioid Treatment Programs.
item.description: Large language model (LLM)-based systems have tremendous potential to improve patient-centered health care, especially for medically underserved populations. However, realizing this potential requires careful consideration of the socio-technical contexts in which LLMs are used. The design of such systems should consider the vulnerabilities of any medically underserved group that the system intends to support, and provide trustworthy evidence for its use.

item.title: Childhood Adversity and Anxiety, Depression, and Suicidal Behaviors Among African-Origin Emerging Adults in the United States: Findings From an Online Panel.
item.description: This study examined associations between adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) and anxiety symptoms, depressive symptoms, lifetime suicidal ideation, and lifetime suicide attempt among African-origin emerging adults in the United States. Data were drawn from a cross-sectional, nonprobability online panel of 537 participants aged 18-29, comprising foreign-born first-generation African immigrants and U.S.-born second-generation participants with African-born parents.

item.title: Adapting peer-delivered behavioral activation for mothers with substance use disorder histories: A peer support specialist co-design study.
item.description: BACKGROUND: Behavioral Activation (BA) is an evidence-based treatment for depression that researchers have adapted for peer delivery to improve access to maternal mental health care. However, little research has examined how peer-delivered BA should be adapted for mothers with substance use disorder (SUD) histories. Building on prior qualitative work with mothers in recovery, this study used Experience-Based Co-Design (EBCD) to adapt the peer-delivered BA intervention Alma in partnership with peer support specialists (PSS) with lived recovery experience.
